reading.body:
IAD39 is a 1.01 million square foot building in Ashburn, Virginia, part of Digital Realty's Northern Virginia campus, one of the largest colocation clusters in the US. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for this facility, making its scale opaque relative to other Virginia data centers. The building offers 2N+1 cooling redundancy, which qualifies it for workloads requiring high availability but does not distinguish its power density or AI suitability.

Virginia has 326 mapped data center facilities, only 23 of which publish power capacity. IAD39 does not publish its megawatts, so it cannot be ranked among the state's disclosed capacity. The 23 Virginia facilities with published figures total 1,375 MW, and this building contributes an unknown share of that total or sits outside it entirely. Without power figures, IAD39's position in Virginia's data center hierarchy cannot be determined from public sources.

The absence of a published power capacity is the binding constraint on assessing whether this campus matters to AI. Colocation buildings of this size typically serve enterprise, cloud, and dense workloads, but without knowing the power envelope, cooling design, or electrical service characteristics, no estimate of AI hosting potential can be made. The operator's publication of street addresses for individual buildings in this Northern Virginia cluster suggests mature, marketed facilities, but the lack of power disclosure for IAD39 specifically places it in the majority of data centers whose contribution to AI scaling remains unmeasured.
